doc.title: Chuck Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 7, 2023

title: Live streaming, home recording and marrying Ria
summary: Lamb discusses technology's effect on livelihood, Caffe Lena streams, home recording, learning tools, and marrying Ria Curley.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: Just to wrap up, the state of music technology and the market and that whole scene. Do you have any observations on it?
How does it — does it affect your livelihood? The fact that well for instance I can watch you and the other people from Small’s, right? A live stream. © Fillius Jazz Archive -18-
I don’t have to pay for it.

That’s a great point. That part is amazing. As we know it that developed full force from the Covid thing you know, the live stream reality. And like the Caffe Lena gig I get people from all over the world tuning in to watch these, so that part of technology is incredible and also just the recording, the whole recording stuff that you can like we’re working on Ria’s new EP, you know and, Ria and I got married on 10/10/21. Or I don’t know if you knew that?

Yeah so I just want to get that on the thing because I love her and it’s incredible to meet somebody you know later on in your life that is your partner and that it’s really cool to be with somebody and you love their music, and the stuff she writes. So we have a blast playing you know her playing piano and singing her tunes and I play acoustic piano and improvise behind it, and then a rhythm section. That’s a really neat vibe. But to be able to put ideas down at home on a recorder and play them back and they sound incredible so to me the home rig, you know, to be able to do that, like that little thing I just played, what if I really dug that I could really put it down and make a beautiful recording, and then I could master it all at home. I mean you know you want to take it up to the studio technology is incredible also. Ultimately you take it there. But I love that stuff man. I think that’s, and as far as a learning tool for kids, for players developing, it’s ridiculous you know that they can access any solo, any recorded solo, Charlie Parker whatever, slow it down you know, it’s instantaneous that’s why — one of the reasons why I think there are so many incredible young players out there, the guys that do it right. It can make you lazy too, make the young players miss some steps. They want to get to — but anyway.
